description: About the Event: WIE CODE is a 12-hour national-level hackathon organized by the WIE IEEE SIT SB. The event aims to bring together innovators, developers, and problem solvers to ideate and build creative tech solutions that empower society through technology. Theme: Empowering society through intelligent innovation Prizes: 1st Prize: ₹15,000 2nd Prize: ₹10,000 Best Female Team: ₹5,000 Best Young Minds: ₹3,000 Best Abstract: ₹2,000 Guidelines: Eligibility: The hackathon is strictly for undergraduate students. Inter-college teams are allowed. Inter-specialization or interdisciplinary teams are encouraged. Team Composition: Team size: 2 to 4 members. Teams must have a female lead. If there are 2 members, both should be girls. If there are 3 members, at least 1 should be a girl. If there are 4 members, at least 2 should be girls. Round 1: Abstract Submission: Teams must submit a detailed abstract/idea document outlining the problem statement, proposed solution, and tech stack. The submission must follow the abstract template provided on the official website. Abstracts will be evaluated based on innovation, feasibility, and societal impact. Round 2: Hackathon: Shortlisted teams will implement their proposed solutions during the 12-hour on-site hackathon. The hackathon will include 3 checkpoints where mentors will review progress and provide guidance. At the end of the hackathon, teams will pitch their project to the judging panel. Rules: Each team must adhere to the submission deadlines; late entries will not be considered. Plagiarism or the use of pre-built solutions will lead to disqualification. Teams should bring their own laptops and required accessories. Internet access and basic technical support will be provided at the venue.

About the Event:

  • WIE CODE is a 12-hour national-level hackathon organized by the WIE IEEE SIT SB.
  • The event aims to bring together innovators, developers, and problem solvers to ideate and build creative tech solutions that empower society through technology.

Theme: Empowering society through intelligent innovation

Prizes:

  • 1st Prize: ₹15,000
  • 2nd Prize: ₹10,000
  • Best Female Team: ₹5,000
  • Best Young Minds: ₹3,000
  • Best Abstract: ₹2,000

Guidelines:

  • Eligibility:
    • The hackathon is strictly for undergraduate students.
    • Inter-college teams are allowed.
    • Inter-specialization or interdisciplinary teams are encouraged.
  • Team Composition:
    • Team size: 2 to 4 members.
    • Teams must have a female lead.
    • If there are 2 members, both should be girls.
    • If there are 3 members, at least 1 should be a girl.
    • If there are 4 members, at least 2 should be girls.

Round 1: Abstract Submission:

  • Teams must submit a detailed abstract/idea document outlining the problem statement, proposed solution, and tech stack.
  • The submission must follow the abstract template provided on the official website.
  • Abstracts will be evaluated based on innovation, feasibility, and societal impact.

Round 2: Hackathon:

  • Shortlisted teams will implement their proposed solutions during the 12-hour on-site hackathon.
  • The hackathon will include 3 checkpoints where mentors will review progress and provide guidance.
  • At the end of the hackathon, teams will pitch their project to the judging panel.

Rules:

  • Each team must adhere to the submission deadlines; late entries will not be considered.
  • Plagiarism or the use of pre-built solutions will lead to disqualification.
  • Teams should bring their own laptops and required accessories.
  • Internet access and basic technical support will be provided at the venue.
